docs.title: Why TinyOlly?
docs.text:
Why send telemetry to a cloud observability platform while coding? Why not have one on your desktop?

TinyOlly is a lightweight OpenTelemetry-native observability platform built from scratch to visualize and correlate logs, metrics, and traces. No 3rd party observability tools - just Python (FastAPI), SQLite, OpenAPI, and JavaScript.

docs.title: Key Features
docs.text:
• Development-focused - Perfect your app's telemetry locally before production
  • Full OpenTelemetry support - Native OTLP ingestion (gRPC & HTTP)
  • Pre-built Docker images - Deploy in ~30 seconds from Docker Hub
  • Runs on Colima - Docker and kind (Kubernetes) on Apple Silicon Macs, no Docker Desktop required
  • Trace correlation - Link logs, metrics, and traces automatically
  • Click-to-copy IDs - Copy trace/span IDs with a single click anywhere in the UI
  • Deep linking - Shareable URLs that open directly to a specific trace (?tab=traces&traceId=...)
  • Trace map - Per-trace service dependency visualization with inferred external client detection
  • Correlated log navigation - Jump from trace detail to filtered logs and vice versa
  • Smart auto-refresh - Auto-refresh pauses when search filters are active, no more losing results
  • Bounded retention - Data expires after 30 minutes by default (SQLITE_TTL_SECONDS) and the database is capped at 256 MB (MAX_DB_SIZE_MB), oldest first
  • Metrics Explorer - Analyze cardinality, labels, and raw series data
  • Service catalog - RED metrics (Rate, Errors, Duration) for all services; click a service name to jump to its map node, traces, spans, logs or metrics
  • Interactive service map - Dependency graph that always fits the window: shape shows service type (server, client, external, database, messaging, isolated), color shows health
  • MCP server - Let Claude Code, Zed or any MCP client query your telemetry, including very large traces (MCP guide)
  • Collector presets - Sampling, PII redaction, enrichment, metrics shaping and more, applied from the UI via OpAMP
  • OpenTelemetry Demo - Run the upstream Astronomy Shop against TinyOlly with one script
  • OpenTelemetry Collector management - Remote configuration management via OpAMP protocol
  • REST API - Programmatic access with OpenAPI documentation
  • Zero vendor lock-in - Works with any OTel Collector distribution

Local Development Only

TinyOlly is not designed to compete with production observability platforms! It's for local development only and is not focused on infrastructure monitoring at this time.

docs.title: Cardinality Protection
docs.text:
Span waterfall showing distributed trace complexity

TinyOlly includes built-in protection against metric cardinality explosion with a configurable limit on unique metric names.

docs.title: Environment Variables
docs.text: Variable Default Description MAX_METRIC_CARDINALITY 1000 Maximum unique metric names SQLITE_TTL_SECONDS 1800 Data retention in seconds (alias: REDIS_TTL)

docs.title: Kubernetes Deployment
docs.text:
Update k8s/tinyolly-otlp-receiver.yaml:

env:
  - name: MAX_METRIC_CARDINALITY
    value: "2000"  # Increase limit
  - name: SQLITE_TTL_SECONDS
    value: "3600"  # 1 hour retention

docs.title: Docker Deployment
docs.text:

environment:
  MAX_METRIC_CARDINALITY: 2000
  SQLITE_TTL_SECONDS: 3600

docs.title: AI Agent Demo
docs.text: This demo showcases GenAI observability with OpenTelemetry - automatic instrumentation of LLM calls using the opentelemetry-instrumentation-ollama package.

docs.title: What is GenAI Observability?
docs.text:
GenAI observability captures telemetry from LLM interactions including:

  • Prompts and responses - Full text of user prompts and model outputs
  • Token usage - Input and output token counts
  • Latency - Response time for each LLM call
  • Model information - Which model was used

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
# Start TinyOlly core first
cd docker
./01-start-core.sh

# Deploy AI agent demo (pulls pre-built images from Docker Hub)
cd ../docker-ai-agent-demo
./01-deploy-ai-demo.sh

This starts:

  • Ollama with TinyLlama model for local LLM inference
  • AI Agent with automatic GenAI span instrumentation

Access the UI at http://localhost:5005 and navigate to the AI Agents tab.

For local development: Use ./01-deploy-ai-demo-local.sh to build locally

Stop: ./02-stop-ai-demo.sh

Cleanup (remove volumes): ./03-cleanup-ai-demo.sh

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
The demo uses zero-code auto-instrumentation - no OpenTelemetry imports in the application code:

# agent.py - NO OpenTelemetry imports needed!
from ollama import Client

client = Client(host="http://ollama:11434")

# This call is AUTO-INSTRUMENTED
response = client.chat(
    model="tinyllama",
    messages=[{"role": "user", "content": "What is OpenTelemetry?"}]
)

The magic happens in the Dockerfile:

# Install auto-instrumentation packages
RUN pip install opentelemetry-distro opentelemetry-instrumentation-ollama

# Run with auto-instrumentation wrapper
CMD ["opentelemetry-instrument", "python", "-u", "agent.py"]

docs.title: What You'll See
docs.text:
In the AI Agents tab:

Field Description Prompt The user's input to the LLM Response The model's output Tokens In Number of input tokens Tokens Out Number of output tokens Latency Response time in milliseconds Model Model name (e.g., tinyllama)

Click any row to expand the full span details in JSON format.

docs.title: Supported LLMs
docs.text:
The OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic conventions work with any instrumented LLM provider:

  • Ollama - Local LLM inference (this demo)
  • OpenAI - GPT models via opentelemetry-instrumentation-openai
  • Anthropic - Claude models
  • Other providers - Any with OpenTelemetry instrumentation

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
No AI traces appearing?

  • Ensure TinyOlly core is running
  • Check agent logs: cd docker-ai-agent-demo && docker compose logs ai-agent
  • Verify Ollama is ready: docker compose logs ollama

Model download taking long?

  • TinyLlama is ~600MB, first download may take a few minutes
  • The Ollama container is limited to 4 GB of RAM, so the default 4 GB Colima VM is too small: restart it larger, e.g. colima stop -p tinyolly && COLIMA_MEMORY=8 ./scripts/colima-up.sh
  • Check Ollama logs for download progress

Agent errors?

  • Ollama needs time to load the model after container starts
  • The agent waits 10 seconds before first call

docs.title: REST API & OpenAPI
docs.text:
OpenAPI documentation with interactive Swagger UI

TinyOlly provides a comprehensive REST API for programmatic access to all telemetry data in OpenTelemetry-native format.

docs.title: Interactive API Documentation
docs.text:
Access the auto-generated OpenAPI documentation: - Swagger UI: http://localhost:5005/docs - Interactive API explorer - ReDoc: http://localhost:5005/redoc - Alternative documentation - OpenAPI Spec: http://localhost:5005/openapi.json - Machine-readable schema

All APIs return OpenTelemetry-native JSON with: - Resources: service.name, host.name, etc. - Attributes: Metric labels and span attributes - Full Context: Trace/span IDs, timestamps, status codes

docs.title: API Endpoints Overview
docs.text:
The REST API provides endpoints for:

Endpoint Method Description /api/traces GET List recent traces with filtering /api/traces/{trace_id} GET Get detailed trace with all spans /api/spans GET List recent spans with filtering /api/logs GET Retrieve logs with trace correlation /api/metrics GET List metrics with type, unit, description and cardinality /api/metrics/query GET Time series for one metric, with resource.* / attribute.* filters and start/end /api/metrics/{name} GET Time series for one metric (no filters) /api/service-map GET Get service dependency graph /api/service-catalog GET List services with RED metrics /api/stats GET System stats and cardinality info /admin/stats GET Detailed admin statistics /health GET Health check endpoint

All endpoints return data in standard OpenTelemetry format, ensuring compatibility with OpenTelemetry tooling and standards.

docs.title: 4. Query Metrics
docs.text:
List the available metrics (metadata only), then fetch one metric's time series:

cURLPython 
# What metrics exist?
curl "http://localhost:5005/api/metrics?limit=100"

# Time series for one metric, last 10 minutes by default (start/end are Unix seconds)
curl "http://localhost:5005/api/metrics/query?name=http.server.duration"

# Filter by resource and metric attributes
curl "http://localhost:5005/api/metrics/query?name=http.server.duration&resource.service.name=demo-frontend&attribute.http.method=GET"

import requests

base = 'http://localhost:5005'
for m in requests.get(f'{base}/api/metrics', params={'limit': 100}).json():
    print(f"{m['name']} ({m['type']}, {m['unit']}) services={m['services']}")

d = requests.get(f'{base}/api/metrics/query',
                 params={'name': 'http.server.duration', 'resource.service.name': 'demo-frontend'}).json()
for s in d['series']:
    print(s['attributes'], [(p['timestamp'], p['value']) for p in s['datapoints'][-3:]])

docs.title: Limits
docs.text:
TinyOlly is designed for local development:

  • Retention: records expire after 30 minutes by default (SQLITE_TTL_SECONDS), and the SQLite database is capped at 256 MB (MAX_DB_SIZE_MB); the oldest records are evicted first when it fills.
  • Cardinality protection limits unique metric names to 1000 (MAX_METRIC_CARDINALITY).
  • Request size: OTLP ingest bodies and gRPC messages are size-capped so a runaway exporter cannot fill the database; very large single batches may need the caps raised (see the receiver's GRPC_MAX_MESSAGE_BYTES).
  • List endpoints accept limit (max 5000).

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text: TinyOlly is a local-only tool and has no authentication, CORS restrictions or origin checks. Do not expose it beyond your machine.

docs.title: Collector presets
docs.text:
TinyOlly ships a baseline collector config plus presets you can apply from the OpenTelemetry Collector + OpAMP Config tab (or POST /api/opamp/config). Each preset is a complete collector config in docker/otelcol-configs/templates/ whose first comment line is the blurb shown in the UI.

Baseline (every config): memory_limiter → resourcedetection (env, system) → batch; the debug exporter is basic verbosity.

Preset Components What you see sampling tail_sampling (errors, >500 ms, 10 % of the rest), probabilistic_sampler (logs 25 %), forward + spanmetrics Trace count drops ~90 %; every error trace is kept. RED metrics are computed before sampling, so rates stay accurate. pii-redaction redaction on traces, logs and metrics (emails, card numbers, bearer tokens, token= URL secrets, *password*/*secret*/*cvv*/*card number* keys), attributes (hash user.id, delete auth/cookie headers; traces and logs) user.email → ****, ?token=… masked, user.id hashed, log bodies masked, redaction.masked.count added. Card patterns only match real card formats (grouped digits, or contiguous Visa/MC/Amex/Discover), so epoch timestamps and numeric IDs are left alone. transform-ottl transform, filter, resource /users/123 → /users/{id}, JSON log bodies flattened to attributes, health checks and debug logs dropped, deployment.environment.name added. enrichment resource, groupbyattrs service.namespace, deployment.environment.name, collector.preset on everything. metrics-shaping deltatocumulative, filter, metricstransform, interval Delta inputs become cumulative, noisy runtime metrics dropped, labels aggregated, 30 s flush. logs-dedup transform, logdedup 60 identical logs → 1 record with dedup_count: 60. connectors-metrics spanmetrics (exemplars on), servicegraph, count, signaltometrics Extra derived metrics: service graph, span/log counts, span-duration histogram. connectors-routing routing, failover, attributes Error spans take their own pipeline (collector.route=errors); failover to a backup exporter. prometheus-remote-write prometheusremotewrite receiver Accepts Prometheus remote write on :19291.

templates/examples/incorrect.yaml is a deliberately broken config for demoing the UI validator; it is not listed as a preset.

docs.title: How configs are applied (important)
docs.text:
The OpAMP supervisor merges the remote config into the base config.yaml (maps are merged by key, lists replaced). Pipelines are therefore merged by name: a preset that only added traces/foo would leave the base traces pipeline running alongside it (so, e.g., sampling would be bypassed). Every preset defines its main pipelines as traces, metrics and logs, and extra pipelines with suffixes (traces/sampled). Keep that convention when writing your own.

Remote config is delivered at the agent's next OpAMP check-in, so a new preset can take ~10-30 s to become active (watch effective config on the Collector tab).

docs.title: Stability notes (collector-contrib 0.165.0)
docs.text: Alpha: filter, redaction (logs/metrics), logdedup, deltatocumulative, count/signaltometrics/routing/failover connectors, probabilistic_sampler (logs). Beta: tail_sampling, transform, memory_limiter, resourcedetection, groupbyattrs, metricstransform, cumulativetodelta. Stable: k8sattributes.

docs.title: Not included (yet)
docs.text:
• k8sattributes (needs RBAC + a Kubernetes cluster) and geoip (needs a MaxMind database) — would be a separate Kubernetes preset.
  • cumulativetodelta and metricstarttime are available in the image but not wired into a preset.
  • filelog receiver (needs file mounts).

docs.title: Development and testing
docs.text:
• Python dependencies are locked: edit requirements.in in a service directory, then regenerate with uv pip compile requirements.in --universal --python-version 3.13 -o requirements.txt.
  • Pinned versions (collector, supervisor, Ollama, OBI, Python, Go) are listed in versions.env; the Dockerfiles carry matching ARG defaults. Update both together.
  • Architecture diagram (docs/images/architecture.png) is generated: edit scripts/make-architecture-diagram.py and run docker/apps/tinyolly-mcp/.venv/bin/python scripts/make-architecture-diagram.py (needs matplotlib and Pillow).
  • Lint: pip install ruff==0.17.4 && ruff check docker/apps/ (rules are in ruff.toml; keep the ruff version pinned, its defaults change between releases). There is no CI; run the checks locally.
  • All local tests: ./scripts/test-all.sh (fast suites; --stack adds the e2e run against the running stack, --kind adds the kind smoke test, which briefly stops the compose stack). Nothing runs in CI. Docs pages need title/description front matter (the MCP server lists them). Suites: common, UI/API, receiver, MCP server, frontend JS (node --test), Go, collector configs, kubectl guard. Individually:
  • Tests: cd docker/apps/tinyolly-common && pip install -r requirements-test.txt . && pytest tests.
  • Go (OpAMP server): ./scripts/test-go.sh (gofmt, vet, go test -race in the pinned golang image). UI tests: cd docker/apps/tinyolly-ui && pytest tests. k8s safety guard: ./scripts/test-kubectx-guard.sh.
  • End-to-end (needs the stack up, ~8 min): python3 scripts/e2e.py (--up starts it, --only a,b picks scenarios, --list). Drives OTLP through the collector, applies every preset via OpAMP, and checks results through the UI API. Test hooks: POST /admin/reset, POST /api/opamp/config?wait=N.
  • Collector configs: ./scripts/test-collector-configs.sh (validate + start every preset); after editing them run ./scripts/sync-k8s-configs.sh.

docs.title: Stack
docs.text:
• Backend: FastAPI (async), SQLite with ZSTD compression + msgpack
  • Frontend: Vanilla JavaScript, HTML, CSS
  • Ingestion: OTLP/gRPC and OTLP/HTTP
  • Storage: 30-minute TTL, sorted sets indexed by timestamp
  • Correlation: Native trace/span/log linking

docs.title: OTLP Support
docs.text:
• Full OpenTelemetry Protocol compliance
  • ResourceSpans, ResourceLogs, ResourceMetrics
  • Spanmetrics integration for RED metrics
  • OpAMP protocol support for remote collector configuration management
  • No vendor lock-in

docs.title: Docker contexts
docs.text: Two Colima VMs can coexist: colima (default) and colima-tinyolly (this project). Every script pins DOCKER_CONTEXT=colima-${COLIMA_PROFILE:-tinyolly} at the top; new scripts that call docker must do the same (copy the 3-line block from any 0N-*.sh). For ad hoc commands use docker --context colima-tinyolly ....

docs.title: Service catalog actions (UI layout, easy revert)
docs.text:
In the APM Service Catalog, per-service actions (Traces, Spans, Logs, Metrics, Service map) are a popover menu opened by clicking the service name. The original layout, a row of buttons on every service, is still in the code.

To revert, set ACTIONS_STYLE = 'buttons' at the top of docker/apps/tinyolly-ui/static/serviceCatalog.js and rebuild the UI image (cd docker && DOCKER_CONTEXT=colima-tinyolly docker compose -f docker-compose-tinyolly-core-local.yml up -d --build --no-deps tinyolly-ui). To remove the menu code entirely, delete SERVICE_ACTIONS, openServiceMenu, closeServiceMenu, the data-service-menu click handler and the two document.addEventListener lines. Map and Service Catalog cross-links (window.viewServiceMap, window.viewServiceCatalog) are independent of this setting.

docs.title: Docker Deployment
docs.text:
Get TinyOlly running on Docker in minutes!

TinyOlly UI showing distributed traces

All examples are launched from the repo - clone it first or download the current GitHub release archive: 

git clone https://github.com/tinyolly/tinyolly

docs.title: 1. Deploy TinyOlly Core (Required)
docs.text:
Start the observability backend (OTel Collector, TinyOlly Receiver, SQLite, UI):

cd docker
./01-start-core.sh

This starts: - OTel Collector: Listening on localhost:4317 (gRPC) and localhost:4318 (HTTP) - OpAMP Server: ws://localhost:4320/v1/opamp (WebSocket), localhost:4321 (HTTP REST API) - TinyOlly UI: http://localhost:5005 - TinyOlly OTLP Receiver and its SQLite storage: OTLP observability back end and storage - Pulls images from Docker Hub (use ./01-start-core-local.sh to build from your checkout instead)

Open the UI: http://localhost:5005 (empty until you send data)

Note

01-start-core.sh starts from a clean slate: it removes the SQLite data volume and the supervisor's cached collector config on every run. Use docker compose -f docker-compose-tinyolly-core.yml restart to keep data.

OpenTelemetry Collector + OpAMP Config Page: Navigate to the "OpenTelemetry Collector + OpAMP Config" tab in the UI to view and manage collector configurations remotely. See the OpAMP Configuration section below for setup instructions.

Stop core services: 

./02-stop-core.sh

docs.title: 2. Deploy Demo Apps (Optional)
docs.text:
Deploy two Flask microservices with automatic traffic generation:

cd docker-demo
./01-deploy-demo.sh

Wait 30 seconds. The demo apps automatically generate traffic - traces, logs, and metrics will appear in the UI!

Stop demo apps: 

./02-cleanup-demo.sh

This leaves TinyOlly core running. To stop everything: 

cd docker
./02-stop-core.sh

docs.title: 3. AI Agent Demo with Ollama (Optional)
docs.text:
Deploy an AI agent demo with zero-code OpenTelemetry auto-instrumentation for GenAI:

cd docker-ai-agent-demo
./01-deploy-ai-demo.sh

Note

First run will pull the Ollama image and TinyLlama model (~1.5GB total). This may take a few minutes.

This starts: - Ollama: Local LLM server with TinyLlama model (http://localhost:11434) - AI Agent: Python agent making LLM calls every 15 seconds, auto-instrumented with opentelemetry-instrumentation-ollama

View AI Traces: Navigate to the AI Agents tab in TinyOlly UI to see:

  • Prompts and responses for each LLM call
  • Token usage (input ↓ / output ↑) with color coding
  • Latency per request
  • Click any row to expand the full span JSON

Watch agent logs: 

docker compose logs -f ai-agent

Stop AI demo: 

./02-stop-ai-demo.sh

Cleanup (remove Ollama model volumes): 

./03-cleanup-ai-demo.sh

docs.title: 4. OpenTelemetry Demo (Astronomy Shop - Optional)
docs.text:
A 16-service subset of the upstream demo, pointed at TinyOlly's collector, with failure-injection feature flags. Runs in ~1.6 GB of VM memory. See OpenTelemetry Demo.

cd docker-otel-demo
./01-start-otel-demo.sh        # shop at http://localhost:8080
./03-set-flag.sh paymentFailure 50%
./02-stop-otel-demo.sh

docs.title: 5. Use TinyOlly with Your Own Apps
docs.text:
After deploying TinyOlly core (step 1 above), instrument your application to send telemetry:

For apps running in Docker containers: Point your OpenTelemetry exporter to: - gRPC: http://otel-collector:4317 - HTTP: http://otel-collector:4318

For apps running on your host machine (outside Docker): Colima forwards container ports to localhost. Point your OpenTelemetry exporter to: - gRPC: http://localhost:4317 - HTTP: http://localhost:4318

Example environment variables: 

export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318

The Otel Collector will forward everything to TinyOlly's OTLP receiver, which processes telemetry and stores it in SQLite in OTEL format for the backend and UI to access.

docs.title: 6. TinyOlly Core-Only Deployment: Use Your Own Docker OpenTelemetry Collector
docs.text:
If you already have an OpenTelemetry Collector or want to send telemetry directly to the TinyOlly Receiver, you can deploy the core components without the bundled OTel Collector.

cd docker-core-only
./01-start-core.sh

This starts: - TinyOlly OTLP Receiver: Listening on localhost:4343 (gRPC only) - OpAMP Server: ws://localhost:4320/v1/opamp (WebSocket), localhost:4321 (HTTP REST API) - TinyOlly UI: http://localhost:5005

Swap out the included Otel Collector for any distro of Otel Collector.

Point your OpenTelemetry exporters to tinyolly-otlp-receiver:4343: i.e. 

exporters:
  debug:
    verbosity: detailed

  otlp:
    endpoint: "tinyolly-otlp-receiver:4343"
    tls:
      insecure: true

service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [debug, otlp, spanmetrics]

    metrics:
      receivers: [otlp,spanmetrics]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [debug, otlp]

    logs:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [debug, otlp]

The Otel Collector will forward everything to TinyOlly's OTLP receiver, which processes telemetry and stores it in SQLite in OTEL format for the backend and UI to access.

docs.title: OpAMP Configuration (Optional)
docs.text:
The OpenTelemetry Collector + OpAMP Config page in the TinyOlly UI allows you to view and manage collector configurations remotely. To enable this feature, add the OpAMP extension to your collector config:

extensions:
  opamp:
    server:
      ws:
        endpoint: ws://localhost:4320/v1/opamp

service:
  extensions: [opamp]

The default configuration template (located at docker/otelcol-configs/config.yaml) shows a complete example with OTLP receivers, OpAMP extension, batch processing, and spanmetrics connector. Your collector will connect to the OpAMP server and receive configuration updates through the TinyOlly UI.

Stop core-only services: 

./02-stop-core.sh

docs.title: Building Images
docs.text: By default, all deployment scripts pull pre-built images from Docker Hub. For building images locally or publishing to Docker Hub, see build/README.md.

docs.title: eBPF Zero-Code Tracing Demo
docs.text: This demo showcases OpenTelemetry eBPF Instrumentation (OBI) - automatic trace capture at the kernel level without any code changes to your application.

docs.title: What is OBI?
docs.text:
OpenTelemetry eBPF Instrumentation (formerly Grafana Beyla) uses eBPF to automatically capture HTTP/gRPC traces by inspecting system calls and network traffic at the Linux kernel level.

Key Benefits: - Zero code changes - no SDK, no agent, no restarts - Language agnostic - works with Python, Go, Java, Node.js, Rust, C, PHP, and more - Protocol-level instrumentation - captures any HTTP/gRPC traffic

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
# Start TinyOlly core first
cd docker
./01-start-core.sh

# Deploy eBPF demo (pulls pre-built images from Docker Hub)
cd ../docker-demo-ebpf
./01-deploy-ebpf-demo.sh

Access the UI at http://localhost:5005

docs.title: Kubernetes
docs.text:
# Start TinyOlly core first
./scripts/colima-up.sh && ./scripts/kind-up.sh
./k8s/02-deploy-tinyolly.sh

# Deploy eBPF demo (pulls pre-built images from Docker Hub)
cd k8s-demo-ebpf
./02-deploy.sh

Access the UI at http://localhost:5005 (kind port mapping)

docs.title: Docker Hub Images
docs.text:
The eBPF demo uses pre-built images from Docker Hub: - tinyolly/ebpf-frontend:latest - Frontend with OTel SDK for metrics/logs - tinyolly/ebpf-backend:latest - Pure Flask backend (no OTel SDK)

For local development, use the build scripts in each demo folder.

docs.title: Traces
Logs
docs.text:
With SDK instrumentation, logs include trace context (trace_id, span_id) for correlation:

{
  "message": "Processing order 12345",
  "trace_id": "abc123...",
  "span_id": "xyz789..."
}

With eBPF instrumentation, logs have no trace context because there's no tracing SDK to inject it:

{
  "message": "Processing order 12345",
  "trace_id": "",
  "span_id": ""
}

This is expected behavior - eBPF operates at the kernel level and cannot inject context into application logs.

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text: Metrics work the same way in both approaches - they're exported via the OTel SDK regardless of how traces are captured.

docs.title: Frontend (ebpf-frontend)
docs.text:
• Flask application with auto-traffic generation
  • Metrics: Exported via OTel SDK (OTLPMetricExporter)
  • Logs: Exported via OTel SDK (OTLPLogExporter)
  • Traces: None from SDK - captured by eBPF agent

docs.title: Backend (ebpf-backend)
docs.text:
• Pure Flask application - no OTel SDK at all
  • Demonstrates that eBPF can trace completely uninstrumented apps
  • Logs go to stdout only (not exported to OTel)

docs.title: eBPF Agent (otel-ebpf-agent)
docs.text:
• Runs with privileged: true and pid: host
  • Monitors port 5000 for HTTP traffic
  • Sends traces to OTel Collector

docs.title: When to Use eBPF vs SDK
docs.text:
Use eBPF when: - You can't modify application code (legacy apps, third-party binaries) - You want basic HTTP observability with zero effort - You're instrumenting many polyglot services quickly

Use SDK when: - You need rich application-level context in traces - You need log-trace correlation - You need custom spans for business logic - You need full distributed tracing with context propagation

Hybrid approach (this demo): - Use eBPF for traces (zero-code) - Use SDK for metrics and logs (richer data)

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
The eBPF agent is configured via environment variables in docker-compose.yml:

otel-ebpf-agent:
  image: docker.io/otel/ebpf-instrument:v1.0.0
  privileged: true
  pid: host
  environment:
    - OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://otel-collector:4317
    - OTEL_EBPF_OPEN_PORT=5000
  volumes:
    - /sys/kernel/debug:/sys/kernel/debug:rw

docs.title: Kubernetes
docs.text:
In Kubernetes, the eBPF agent runs as a DaemonSet to instrument all pods on each node:

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: DaemonSet
metadata:
  name: otel-ebpf-agent
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      hostPID: true
      containers:
      - name: ebpf-agent
        image: docker.io/otel/ebpf-instrument:v1.0.0
        securityContext:
          privileged: true
        env:
        - name: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT
          value: "http://otel-collector:4317"
        - name: OTEL_EBPF_OPEN_PORT
          value: "5000"
        volumeMounts:
        - name: sys-kernel-debug
          mountPath: /sys/kernel/debug
      volumes:
      - name: sys-kernel-debug
        hostPath:
          path: /sys/kernel/debug

docs.title: Key Settings
docs.text:
• OTEL_EBPF_OPEN_PORT: Which port to monitor (5000 = Flask default)
  • privileged: true: Required for eBPF kernel access
  • hostPID: true / pid: host: Required to see processes in other containers/pods

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
No traces appearing? - Ensure TinyOlly core is running (docker ps | grep otel-collector) - Check eBPF agent logs: docker logs otel-ebpf-instrumentation (run against the colima-tinyolly context: DOCKER_CONTEXT=colima-tinyolly docker logs ...) - Verify the agent can access /sys/kernel/debug

Traces have wrong service name? - OBI discovers service names from process info - Set OTEL_EBPF_SERVICE_NAME for explicit naming

eBPF agent won't start? - Requires Linux kernel 4.4+ with eBPF support - On macOS it runs inside the Colima Linux VM. This demo has not been verified on Colima's default vz VM type; if the agent fails to start, check its logs and whether the VM kernel exposes /sys/kernel/debug - The agent runs privileged with the host PID namespace (required for eBPF)

docs.text:

  • OBI GitHub Repository
  • OBI Docker Setup Guide

docs.title: Kubernetes Deployment
docs.text:
Deploy TinyOlly on Kubernetes (kind on Colima) for local development!

Service map showing microservices running on Kubernetes

All examples are launched from the repo - clone it first or download the current GitHub release archive: 

git clone https://github.com/tinyolly/tinyolly

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Colima, docker, kind, kubectl
brew install colima docker docker-compose docker-buildx docker-credential-helper kubectl kind helm

docs.title: 1. Deploy TinyOlly Core
docs.text:
1. Start Colima and the kind cluster:

    ./scripts/colima-up.sh   # defaults: 4 CPU / 4 GB (COLIMA_MEMORY=8 for more)
./scripts/kind-up.sh

  2. Deploy TinyOlly:

    Images will be pulled from Docker Hub automatically:

    ./k8s/02-deploy-tinyolly.sh

    Alternatively, you can manually apply all manifests with kubectl apply -f k8s/

    Local Development Build (Optional)

    To build images locally and load them into kind instead of pulling from Docker Hub: 

    ./build/local/build-core-kind.sh

  3. Access the UI:

    The UI is a NodePort service mapped to the host by scripts/kind-config.yaml (no tunnel needed). Access the TinyOlly UI at: http://localhost:5005

    OpenTelemetry Collector + OpAMP Config Page: Navigate to the "OpenTelemetry Collector + OpAMP Config" tab in the UI to view and manage collector configurations remotely. See the OpAMP Configuration section below for setup instructions.

  4. Send Telemetry from Host Apps:

    No port-forward is needed: scripts/kind-config.yaml maps the collector's NodePorts to your host. Point your application's OpenTelemetry exporter to: - gRPC: http://localhost:4317 - HTTP: http://localhost:4318

    (These host ports are shared with the Docker stack, so run one or the other at a time.)

    Example environment variables: 

    export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318

    For apps running inside the Kubernetes cluster: Use the Kubernetes service name: - gRPC: http://otel-collector:4317 - HTTP: http://otel-collector:4318

  5. Clean Up:

    Use the cleanup script to remove all TinyOlly resources:

    ./k8s/03-cleanup.sh

    Delete the kind cluster and stop Colima: 

    kind delete cluster --name tinyolly
colima stop -p tinyolly

docs.title: 2. Demo Applications (Optional)
docs.text:
To see TinyOlly in action with instrumented microservices (deploy the full core from step 1 first; the demo sends to its collector):

cd k8s-demo
./02-deploy.sh

The deploy script pulls demo images from Docker Hub by default. For local development, you can build images locally when prompted.

To clean up the demo: 

./03-cleanup.sh

The demo includes two microservices that automatically generate traffic, showcasing distributed tracing across service boundaries.

docs.title: 3. OpenTelemetry Demo (~20 Services - Optional)
docs.text:
To deploy the full OpenTelemetry Demo with ~20 microservices:

Prerequisites: - TinyOlly must be deployed first (see Setup above) - Helm installed - Sufficient cluster resources (demo is resource-intensive)

Deploy: 

cd k8s-otel-demo
./01-deploy-otel-demo-helm.sh

Warning

The Helm-based OpenTelemetry Demo and the k8s-demo-ebpf / k8s-ai-agent-demo folders were converted from minikube to kind but have not been run end to end yet. The Docker versions are the tested path. For the OpenTelemetry Demo, prefer the Docker version.

This deploys all OpenTelemetry Demo services configured to send telemetry to TinyOlly's collector via HTTP on port 4318. Built-in observability tools (Jaeger, Grafana, Prometheus) are disabled.

Cleanup: 

cd k8s-otel-demo
./02-cleanup-otel-demo-helm.sh

This removes the OpenTelemetry Demo but leaves TinyOlly running.

docs.title: 4. TinyOlly Core-Only Deployment: Use Your Own Kubernetes OpenTelemetry Collector
docs.text:
To deploy TinyOlly without the bundled OTel Collector (e.g., if you have an existing collector daemonset). Includes OpAMP server for optional remote collector configuration management:

  1. Deploy Core: 

    cd k8s-core-only
./01-deploy.sh

  2. Access UI: Access http://localhost:5005 (kind port mapping).

  3. Cleanup: 

    ./02-cleanup.sh

docs.title: Use TinyOlly with Any OpenTelemetry Collector
docs.text:
Swap out the included Otel Collector for any distro of Otel Collector.

Point your OpenTelemetry exporters to tinyolly-otlp-receiver:4343: i.e. 

exporters:
  debug:
    verbosity: detailed

  otlp:
    endpoint: "tinyolly-otlp-receiver:4343"
    tls:
      insecure: true

service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [debug, otlp, spanmetrics]

    metrics:
      receivers: [otlp,spanmetrics]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [debug, otlp]

    logs:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
      exporters: [debug, otlp]

The Otel Collector will forward everything to TinyOlly's OTLP receiver, which processes telemetry and stores it in SQLite in OTEL format for the backend and UI to access.

docs.title: OpAMP Configuration (Optional)
docs.text:
The OpenTelemetry Collector + OpAMP Config page in the TinyOlly UI allows you to view and manage collector configurations remotely. To enable this feature, add the OpAMP extension to your collector config:

extensions:
  opamp:
    server:
      ws:
        endpoint: ws://tinyolly-opamp-server:4320/v1/opamp

service:
  extensions: [opamp]

The default configuration template (included as a ConfigMap in k8s-core-only/tinyolly-opamp-server.yaml) shows a complete example with OTLP receivers, OpAMP extension, batch processing, and spanmetrics connector. Your collector will connect to the OpAMP server and receive configuration updates through the TinyOlly UI.

docs.title: MCP server (AI agents)
docs.text: docker/apps/tinyolly-mcp is a small, read-only MCP server. It lets Claude Code, Zed or any MCP client query the telemetry in your running TinyOlly (traces, spans, logs, metrics, the service catalog and the service map) and read these docs, so an agent can also answer "how do I set up / configure / use TinyOlly?". It is telemetry only: no collector config or admin operations.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
docker/apps/tinyolly-mcp/install.sh     # creates .venv and prints the registration command

claude mcp add tinyolly -- /path/to/tinyolly/docker/apps/tinyolly-mcp/.venv/bin/python /path/to/tinyolly/docker/apps/tinyolly-mcp/server.py

TinyOlly must be running (http://localhost:5005; override with TINYOLLY_URL). For HTTP instead of stdio: python server.py --http --port 8765, then register http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp (e.g. claude mcp add --transport http tinyolly http://127.0.0.1:8765/mcp).

docs.title: Tools
docs.text:
Tool What it does list_services Service catalog with rate, error rate, p50/p95/p99, worst errors first (format="table" for a pretty table) get_service_map Compact caller → callee edges search_traces Recent traces filtered by service, errors, min duration, root name (format="table") get_trace Bounded summary of a trace: duration, counts, per-service breakdown, error spans, slowest spans, depth. format="waterfall" draws a text waterfall get_trace_spans Page through a trace's spans (offset/limit, service/error/duration filters) get_span Full detail of one span (attributes, events, links, resource) search_spans Recent spans across traces filtered by service, errors, duration, name (format="table") query_logs Logs by trace, service, severity, substring (format="table") list_metrics Metric names with a search filter query_metric Time series for the last N minutes, downsampled with min/max/avg/last chart_metric Image: line chart of a metric (histograms: mean solid, p95 dashed), series labelled by what differs between them chart_service_map Image: one service's dependencies, callers left and callees right, colored by health, edges labelled with p95 and request rate (depth=2 for two hops) list_skills Investigation skills (playbooks): when to use each get_skill The full steps of one skill list_docs These documentation pages: name, title, description, section headings search_docs Search the docs; returns matching sections with snippets read_doc Read a page or just one section (paged if long)

The same pages are also exposed as MCP resources: tinyolly-docs://<name> (for example tinyolly-docs://quickstart).

docs.title: Pretty output and visuals
docs.text:
The JSON tools are compact for agents. When you want something to show a person, pass format="table" (catalog, traces, spans, logs: markdown tables with health and severity icons, readable durations and times) or format="waterfall" on get_trace (indented span tree with timing bars; big traces keep every error span plus the slowest spans, up to max_rows). chart_metric and chart_service_map return PNG images, so the client must display image results (Claude Desktop and Claude Code do). Charts are drawn with matplotlib, which install.sh installs into the server's venv.

Try asking: "chart http.server.duration for tinyolly-ui", "draw the service map around cart", "show the slowest checkout trace as a waterfall", "pretty print the service catalog".

docs.title: Investigation skills
docs.text:
Six short skills teach an agent how to investigate with these tools. They live only inside the MCP server (docker/apps/tinyolly-mcp/skills/); nothing is installed into Claude Code or any other client.

Skill Use it for tinyolly-triage "What is wrong right now?": rank services, find a failing trace, report where/what/evidence/next tinyolly-trace-investigation One trace: summary, waterfall, paging huge traces, self-time vs first-error reasoning tinyolly-service-deep-dive One service: vitals, dependency map, errors, slow traces, logs, metrics tinyolly-metrics-explorer Finding, charting and interpreting metrics (counters, gauges, histograms, cardinality) tinyolly-troubleshoot-stack TinyOlly itself is empty or unreachable (Colima contexts, ports, retention) and setup questions tinyolly-demo-failure-injection Break the OTel demo with a feature flag and watch TinyOlly catch it

The server offers them three ways, so any MCP client can use them:

  • Tools: list_skills and get_skill(name). The server's instructions tell agents to call list_skills before an investigation.
  • Prompts: one prompt per skill with an optional focus argument (shows up as a slash command or prompt picker where the client supports it), e.g. tinyolly-triage with focus "checkout is slow".
  • Resources: tinyolly-skills://<name>.

The tests check that every tool and parameter a skill mentions really exists, so a skill cannot silently drift from the tools. Add one by creating skills/<name>.md with name (same as the file name) and a description that starts with "Use when".

docs.title: Docs
docs.text:
The server reads docs/*.md from the repo (override the location with TINYOLLY_DOCS_DIR). Pages are cleaned for agents: screenshots and HTML layout removed, mkdocs admonitions and tabs flattened to plain markdown, and each page is split by heading so read_doc(name, section) returns only what is needed. Every page starts with title and description front matter, which is what list_docs shows, so keep that when adding a page.

Try asking: "how do I run the OpenTelemetry demo?", "which collector presets exist and what do they do?", "what ports does TinyOlly use?".

docs.title: Large traces
docs.text:
Nothing returns an unbounded payload. Drill down instead of dumping: search_traces → get_trace (summary, a few KB even for a 6,000-span trace) → get_trace_spans (pages of up to 200 compact rows) → get_span for one span. Attribute values and log bodies are truncated, series are downsampled, and every response is hard-capped at TINYOLLY_MCP_MAX_CHARS (default 20,000) with a truncated flag telling the agent to narrow the query.

Try asking: "which services have the highest error rate?", "find the slowest checkout trace and tell me where the time went", "show error logs for the cart service".

docs.title: Metrics & Cardinality explorer
docs.text: TinyOlly provides a powerful interface for analyzing OpenTelemetry metrics, with specific tools designed to help you understand the shape and cardinality of your telemetry data.

docs.title: Metrics Table
docs.text:
The metrics table offers a dense, high-information view of all ingested metrics.

Click the Chart button to visualize metric data over time:

docs.title: Key Columns
docs.text:
• Name: The full OTel metric name (e.g., http.server.response.size).
  • Unit: The unit of measurement (e.g., By, ms).
  • Type: The metric type (Histogram, Sum, Gauge, etc.).
  • Resources: Click to view the unique resource combinations associated with this metric.
  • Cardinality: Shows the number of label dimensions vs the total number of unique time series (e.g., 8 labels / 185 series).

docs.title: Cardinality Explorer
docs.text: Clicking on the blue Cardinality link for any metric opens the Cardinality Explorer. This tool is essential for understanding "high cardinality" issues and exploring your data's dimensions.

docs.title: 1. Header Stats
docs.text:
• Total Series (Historic): The total number of unique time series seen for this metric since startup (persisted in SQLite).
  • Active Series (1h): The count of series seen in the last hour.
  • Label Dimensions: The number of unique label keys (e.g., http.method, http.status_code).

docs.title: 2. Label Analysis Table
docs.text:
This table helps you identify which labels are contributing most to your cardinality.

  • Label Name: The key of the label.
  • Cardinality: The number of unique values for this label.
  • Values (Top 5): A preview of the most common values.
    • If there are more than 5 values, a clickable ... link expands the list to show all values inline.

docs.title: 3. Raw Active Series
docs.text:
A scrollable view of all active series in a PromQL-like syntax:

{container.id="...", http.method="GET", http.route="/api/traces", http.status_code="200", service.name="tinyolly-ui"}
{container.id="...", http.method="GET", http.route="/health", http.status_code="200", service.name="tinyolly-ui"}

docs.title: Export Actions
docs.text:
Use the buttons in the "Raw Active Series" section to export data for offline analysis:

  • Copy PromQL: Copies the visible series list to your clipboard.
  • Download JSON: Downloads the full series object as a JSON file.

docs.title: Cardinality Protection
docs.text:
TinyOlly includes built-in protection against cardinality explosions to prevent memory exhaustion during local development.

  • Hard Limit: 1000 unique metric names (MAX_METRIC_CARDINALITY).
  • Visual Warning: the Metrics tab shows count/1000, which turns red with a ⚠️ at 80% of the limit (the display assumes the default 1000).
  • Behavior: Metrics exceeding the limit are dropped, and a system alert is triggered.

See Cardinality Protection for more details.

docs.title: OpenTelemetry Collector
docs.text:
OpenTelemetry Collector configuration management via OpAMP

TinyOlly uses the OpenTelemetry Collector as the telemetry ingestion and shipping layer. The collector receives telemetry from your applications and forwards it to TinyOlly's OTLP receiver.

docs.title: OpenTelemetry Collector + OpAMP Config Page
docs.text:
TinyOlly includes a web interface for managing OpenTelemetry Collector configurations via the OpAMP (Open Agent Management Protocol). Access this page through the "OpenTelemetry Collector + OpAMP Config" tab in the TinyOlly UI.

Features: - View current configuration from connected collectors - Apply configuration changes with real-time validation - Browse configuration templates for common use cases - Monitor OpAMP server status and connected agents - Preview configuration diffs before applying

Requirements: - Your collector must be configured with the OpAMP extension (see OpAMP Configuration below) - Collector must be connected to the OpAMP server

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
TinyOlly includes a sample collector configuration that you can customize for your needs. The configuration files are located at:

  • Docker: docker/otelcol-configs/config.yaml (the single source of truth)
  • Kubernetes: k8s/otelcol-configs/config.yaml, a ConfigMap generated from the Docker config by scripts/sync-k8s-configs.sh

docs.title: Default Configuration
docs.text:
The default configuration includes:

  • OTLP Receivers: Accepts telemetry on ports 4317 (gRPC) and 4318 (HTTP)
  • OpAMP Extension: Enables remote configuration management via TinyOlly UI
  • Span Metrics Connector: Automatically generates RED metrics from traces
  • Batch Processor: Batches telemetry for efficient processing
  • OTLP Exporter: Forwards all telemetry to TinyOlly's OTLP receiver

docs.title: Customization Examples
docs.text:
You can extend the collector configuration to add additional capabilities. The collector uses the otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib image which includes:

  • Receivers: OTLP, Prometheus, Jaeger, Zipkin, and many more
  • Processors: Batch, Memory Limiter, Resource Detection, Tail Sampling, Filtering
  • Connectors: Span Metrics, Service Graph
  • Exporters: OTLP, Prometheus, Logging, and many more

For a complete list of available components, see the OpenTelemetry Collector Contrib documentation.

docs.title: Docker
docs.text:
After modifying docker/otelcol-configs/config.yaml rebuild/restart using: 

cd docker
./01-start-core.sh

docs.title: Kubernetes
docs.text:
Edit docker/otelcol-configs/config.yaml, regenerate the ConfigMaps, and restart the collector: 

./scripts/sync-k8s-configs.sh
kubectl apply -f k8s/otelcol-configs/
kubectl rollout restart deployment/otel-collector

docs.title: Using Your Own Collector
docs.text:
You can use your own OpenTelemetry Collector instance instead of the one bundled with TinyOlly. This is useful if you have an existing collector setup or want to test specific collector configurations.

To do this, deploy the Core-Only version of TinyOlly (see Docker Deployment or Kubernetes Deployment).

Then, configure your collector's OTLP exporter to send data to the TinyOlly Receiver:

  • Endpoint: tinyolly-otlp-receiver:4343 (or localhost:4343 from host)
  • Protocol: gRPC
  • TLS: Insecure (or configured as needed)

Example Exporter Configuration: 

exporters:
  otlp:
    endpoint: "tinyolly-otlp-receiver:4343"
    tls:
      insecure: true

docs.title: OpAMP Configuration (Optional)
docs.text:
The OpenTelemetry Collector + OpAMP Config page in the TinyOlly UI allows you to view and manage collector configurations remotely. To enable this feature, add the OpAMP extension to your collector config:

extensions:
  opamp:
    server:
      ws:
        endpoint: ws://localhost:4320/v1/opamp

service:
  extensions: [opamp]

The default configuration template (located at docker/otelcol-configs/config.yaml) shows a complete example with OTLP receivers, OpAMP extension, batch processing, and spanmetrics connector. Your collector will connect to the OpAMP server and receive configuration updates through the TinyOlly UI.

docs.title: OpenTelemetry Demo (Astronomy Shop) with TinyOlly
docs.text:
TinyOlly's realistic demo is the upstream OpenTelemetry Demo ("Astronomy Shop", pinned to OTEL_DEMO_VERSION in versions.env). We run a 16-service subset (frontend, proxy, cart + Valkey, checkout, payment, shipping, currency, quote, email, ad, recommendation, product catalog + Postgres, image provider, flagd) plus a light Locust load generator. Everything exports OTLP to TinyOlly's collector; the demo's own collector, Jaeger, Grafana, Prometheus, OpenSearch, Kafka and its consumers are not started.

Footprint: ~1.1 GB of containers for demo + TinyOlly, ~1.6 GB used inside the Colima VM (4 GB default), so it runs on an 8 GB Mac.

# 1. One-time prerequisites (macOS)
brew install colima docker docker-compose docker-buildx docker-credential-helper git
mkdir -p ~/.docker && echo '{"cliPluginsExtraDirs": ["/opt/homebrew/lib/docker/cli-plugins"]}' > ~/.docker/config.json   # merge into an existing file if you have one

# 2. Get TinyOlly and start its Colima VM
git clone https://github.com/tinyolly/tinyolly.git && cd tinyolly
./scripts/colima-up.sh                  # VM 'tinyolly' (Docker context: colima-tinyolly); COLIMA_MEMORY=6 ./scripts/colima-up.sh for more headroom

# 3. Start TinyOlly core (UI :5005, OTLP :4317/:4318)
(cd docker && ./01-start-core.sh)       # use ./01-start-core-local.sh to build from this checkout instead

# 4. Start the OpenTelemetry Demo (first run pulls ~16 images)
cd docker-otel-demo
./01-start-otel-demo.sh                 # clones opentelemetry-demo into .demo/ and starts a 16-service subset

# 5. Use it
open http://localhost:8080              # the shop
open http://localhost:5005              # TinyOlly
./03-set-flag.sh                        # list failure-injection flags
./03-set-flag.sh paymentFailure 50%     # inject failures
./03-set-flag.sh --reset                # turn all flags off

# 6. Stop
./02-stop-otel-demo.sh                  # demo only; add --purge to delete the .demo/ clone

No config edits are needed. The script clones the demo at the pinned version and points every service at TinyOlly's collector (host.docker.internal:4317).

Options: LOADGEN=0 (no load generator), LOCUST_USERS=3, SERVICES="..." (custom service list).

docs.title: Failure injection with feature flags
docs.text:
The demo reads feature flags from flagd. ./03-set-flag.sh <flag> <variant> edits the flag file (flagd hot-reloads it); ./03-set-flag.sh --reset turns everything off. Flags with a Preset column pair with a collector preset.

Flag Try What to look at Preset paymentFailure 50% / 100% Verified. payment and checkout error rates in Service Catalog; error traces list with ERR; checkout returns 422 PAYMENT_FAILED sampling keeps every error trace emitRawPii on Verified. raw user.email, demo.payment.card_number, demo.payment.card_cvv on spans pii-redaction masks them (****), hashes user.id cartFailure 25% … 100% cart errors, failing add-to-cart sampling productCatalogFailure on errors for one product, visible in the trace map connectors-metrics (service graph) imageSlowLoad, intlShippingSlowdown 5sec / 10sec slow spans, latency percentiles sampling (keeps >500 ms traces) adHighCpu, adManualGc, emailMemoryLeak on / 10x resource metrics on the affected service metrics-shaping loadGeneratorFloodHomepage on request flood. Do not use on an 8 GB machine without watching docker stats sampling, metrics-shaping

Entries not marked Verified are expected behaviour from the flag descriptions and have not been checked against TinyOlly yet. Flags that depend on Kafka (kafkaQueueProblems), the AI agent (ai*) or flagd-ui are not available in this subset.

docs.title: Notes
docs.text:
• Image tags: the demo's .env defaults DEMO_VERSION=latest (images from main), which does not match the checked-out compose file (the newer recommendation image has no nc, so its healthcheck fails). The script pins DEMO_VERSION to the git tag.
  • The demo is cloned to docker-otel-demo/.demo/ (git-ignored); ./02-stop-otel-demo.sh --purge removes it.
  • Kubernetes: k8s-otel-demo/01-deploy-otel-demo-helm.sh installs chart 0.42.6 (app 3.1.0). The chart also deploys Kafka and its consumers (checkout waits for Kafka), so it needs a VM of 6 GB or more. Not tested on kind yet.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text: Get TinyOlly running in under 5 minutes!

docs.title: What You'll Get
docs.text:
• TinyOlly UI at http://localhost:5005
  • OpenTelemetry Collector listening on ports 4317 (gRPC) and 4318 (HTTP)
  • OpAMP Server for remote collector configuration management
  • Demo microservices generating automatic telemetry

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Colima + docker CLI installed and running (brew install colima docker docker-compose docker-buildx docker-credential-helper, then ./scripts/colima-up.sh). The scripts use the colima-tinyolly Docker context, so they work even if another Docker context or VM is active
  • Git (to clone the repository)
  • 5 minutes of your time

docs.title: Step 1: Clone the Repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/tinyolly/tinyolly
cd tinyolly

docs.title: Step 2: Start TinyOlly Core
docs.text:
cd docker
./01-start-core.sh

This pulls pre-built images from Docker Hub and starts:

  • OpenTelemetry Collector (ports 4317/4318)
  • OpAMP Server (ports 4320/4321)
  • TinyOlly OTLP Receiver (internal)
  • TinyOlly UI (port 5005)
  • SQLite storage (embedded)

Deployment time: ~30 seconds (pulls from Docker Hub)

For local development: Use ./01-start-core-local.sh to build images locally.

docs.title: Step 3: Deploy Demo Apps (Optional but Recommended)
docs.text:
In a new terminal:

cd docker-demo
./01-deploy-demo.sh

This pulls demo images from Docker Hub and deploys two Flask microservices that automatically generate traffic.

Wait 30 seconds for telemetry to appear!

For local development: Use ./01-deploy-demo-local.sh to build images locally.

docs.title: Step 4: Open the UI
docs.text:
Open your browser to: http://localhost:5005

You should see:

Trace waterfall with correlated logs and span timing

docs.title: Traces Tab
docs.text:
View distributed traces across microservices with timing waterfall.

Span waterfall showing request timing breakdown with correlated logs

Click on a span to view detailed JSON data:

Span detail view with full OpenTelemetry attributes

docs.title: Logs Tab
docs.text:
Browse logs with trace/span correlation. Filter by severity (Error, Warn, Info, Debug).

Real-time logs with trace and span correlation

Click on a log entry to view full details:

Log detail view with full attributes and resource info

Filter to show only errors:

Filtered error logs with trace correlation

docs.title: Metrics Tab
docs.text:
Visualize metrics with automatic charting.

Time-series metrics visualization with rate charts

docs.title: Service Catalog
docs.text:
View all services with RED metrics (Rate, Errors, Duration). Click a service name for a menu that jumps to its map node, traces, spans, logs or metrics.

Service catalog with RED metrics for all services

docs.title: Service Map
docs.text:
Visualize service dependencies with an interactive graph. Shape shows the service type and color shows health (see the legend above the map); click a node for latency and a link to the Service Catalog, and use the checkbox to hide TinyOlly's own services.

Interactive service dependency map with latency information

docs.title: OpenTelemetry Collector + OpAMP Config
docs.text:
View and manage your OpenTelemetry Collector configuration remotely via the OpAMP protocol.

OpenTelemetry Collector configuration management via OpAMP

This page allows you to:

  • View current configuration from connected collectors
  • Apply configuration changes with validation and diff preview
  • Use collector presets for common scenarios (sampling, PII redaction, transforms, connectors, prometheus-remote-write...); see Collector presets
  • Check OpAMP server status and see connected collector agents
  • Validate configurations before applying to catch errors early

To use this feature, your OpenTelemetry Collector must be configured with the OpAMP extension (see Docker Deployment or OpenTelemetry Collector documentation).

docs.title: Step 6: Use Your Own Application
docs.text:
Point your application's OpenTelemetry exporter to:

For apps running on your host machine (outside Docker): 

export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://localhost:4318

For apps running inside Docker: 

export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://otel-collector:4318

TinyOlly will automatically capture and display your telemetry!

docs.title: Cleanup
docs.text:
Stop demo apps (keeps TinyOlly running): 

cd docker-demo
./02-cleanup-demo.sh

Stop everything: 

cd docker
./02-stop-core.sh

docs.text:

  • Explore the REST API at http://localhost:5005/docs
  • Deploy on Kubernetes
  • Learn about the architecture

docs.title: UI shows "No traces/logs/metrics"
docs.text:
• Wait 30 seconds after starting demo apps
  • Check containers are running in the TinyOlly VM: docker --context colima-tinyolly ps (plain docker ps shows whichever context is active, possibly another Colima VM)
  • Check demo app logs: docker compose -f docker-demo/docker-compose-demo.yml logs

docs.title: Port conflicts
docs.text:
• TinyOlly uses ports 4317, 4318, 4320, 4321, 4343, 5005, 19291
  • Stop conflicting services or modify ports in docker-compose-tinyolly-core.yml

docs.title: Demo apps not generating traffic
docs.text:
• Restart demo: cd docker-demo && ./02-cleanup-demo.sh && ./01-deploy-demo.sh
  • Check logs: docker compose -f docker-demo/docker-compose-demo.yml logs demo-frontend

For more help, open an issue on GitHub.

docs.title: Data Storage
docs.text:
• Format: Full OpenTelemetry (OTEL) format for traces, logs, and metrics
  • SQLite: All telemetry stored in an embedded SQLite database (compressed with ZSTD + msgpack)
  • WAL Mode: Write-Ahead Logging for concurrent reads during writes
  • Retention: Records expire after 30 minutes by default (SQLITE_TTL_SECONDS), and the database is also capped at 256 MB (MAX_DB_SIZE_MB); when full, the oldest records are evicted first
  • Correlation: Native trace-metric-log correlation via trace/span IDs
  • Cardinality Protection: Prevents metric explosion
  • Ephemeral by Design: Designed for local development — data persists across restarts until it expires or storage fills up

docs.title: OTLP Compatibility
docs.text: TinyOlly is fully OpenTelemetry-native: - Ingestion: Accepts OTLP/gRPC (primary) and OTLP/HTTP - Storage: Stores traces, logs, and metrics in full OTEL format with resources, scopes, and attributes - Correlation: Native support for trace/span ID correlation across all telemetry types - REST API: Exposes OTEL-formatted JSON for programmatic access - Control Plane: OpenTelemetry Collector OpAmp for dynamic configuration

docs.title: UI Features
docs.text:
• Trace Waterfall: Distributed trace visualization with automatic filtering of noisy ASGI sub-spans (http send/receive)
  • Trace Map: Per-trace service dependency graph rendered above the waterfall using Cytoscape.js. Detects inferred external clients from orphan parent span IDs (e.g., test clients that propagate trace context but don't export spans)
  • Deep Linking: Shareable URLs that open directly to a specific trace detail view (?tab=traces&traceId=...), span search (?tab=spans&spanId=...), or filtered tab (?tab=logs&search=...). "Copy Link" buttons in trace and span detail views generate these URLs
  • Click-to-Copy IDs: Trace and span IDs are copyable with a single click throughout the UI
  • Correlated Logs: Trace detail view shows correlated logs inline — click any log row to navigate to the Logs tab filtered by trace ID
  • Cross-Tab Navigation: Click trace/span IDs in logs to jump to the corresponding trace or span view
  • Service Catalog: RED metrics; clicking a service name opens a menu (Service map, Traces, Spans, Logs, Metrics) filtered to that service
  • Service Map: Cytoscape.js dependency graph laid out left-to-right (dagre), sized to always fit the window. Shape = service type (server, client, external, database, messaging, isolated), color = health (blue healthy, amber some errors, red >5% errors). Isolated services sit in a grid to the right; an option hides TinyOlly's own services. Selecting a node shows P50/P95/P99 latency and rate with a link back to the catalog
  • Smart Auto-Refresh: 5-second polling pauses automatically when a search filter is active, preventing result disruption
  • Scrollable Lists: Trace, span, and log lists support scrolling with sticky headers for large datasets

docs.title: MCP Server
docs.text: docker/apps/tinyolly-mcp is a read-only MCP server over the REST API (traces, spans, logs, metrics, service catalog/map) that also serves these docs (list_docs, search_docs, read_doc) renders pretty tables, a trace waterfall and PNG charts (metrics, single-service map), and ships investigation skills (skills/) that it serves as MCP tools, prompts and resources. Every response is size-bounded; large traces are summarized and paged. See the MCP guide.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text: Everything runs locally (no CI): ./scripts/test-all.sh runs the unit suites (storage library, UI/API, OTLP receiver, MCP server, frontend JS, OpAMP Go server, collector configs, kubectl-context guard). --stack adds an end-to-end run against the live stack (88 checks including every collector preset) and --kind adds a Kubernetes smoke test on kind. See the development notes.
